regulations.name: IEC 60825-1:2007
regulations.scope: Lasers, laser light barriers, wavelength range 180nm to 1mm

tests.requirement: RISK from unintended X-radiation from ME EQUIPMENT producing X-radiation for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes
RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS as indicated in RISK MANAGEMENT FILE
RISK associated with alpha, beta, gamma, neutron, and other particle radiation addressed in RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS
Power density of unintended microwave radiation at frequencies between 1 GHz and 100 GHz does not exceed 10 W/m2 at any point 50 mm away from a surface of ME EQUIPMENT under reference test conditions
Microwave radiation propagated intentionally (e.g. at waveguide output ports)
Relevant requirements of IEC 60825-1:2007 applied to lasers, laser light barriers or similar with wavelength range 180nm to 1mm
RISK associated with visible electromagnetic radiation other than emitted by lasers and LEDS addressed in RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS
RISK associated with infrared radiation other than emitted by lasers and LEDS addressed in RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS
RISK associated with ultraviolet radiation other than emitted by lasers and LEDS addressed in RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS
PROTECTION AGAINST EXCESSIVE TEMPERATURES AND OTHER HAZARDS
Excessive temperatures in ME EQUIPMENT
Temperatures on ME EQUIPMENT parts did not exceed values in Tables 22 and 23 operating in worst-case NORMAL USE at maximum rated ambient operating temperature T
Surfaces of test corner did not exceed 90°C
THERMAL CUT-OUTS did not operate in NORMAL CONDITION
Temperature of APPLIED PARTS
APPLIED PARTS (hot or cold) intended to supply heat to a PATIENT comply
tests.result: Applied parts did not intend to supply heat to a patient.

tests.requirement: Clinical effects determined and documented in RISK MANAGEMENT FILE (ISO 14971 Cl. 4.2-4.4, 5, 6.2-6.5)
Temperature (hot or cold) of APPLIED PARTS intended to supply heat to PATIENT disclosed in instructions for use
APPLIED PARTS not intended to supply heat to PATIENT complies with limits of Table 24 in both NORMAL CONDITION and SINGLE FAULT CONDITION
APPLIED PARTS surface temperature exceeds 41°C disclosed in the instruction manual
APPLIED PARTS surface temperature equal to or less than 41°C

Analysis documented in RISK MANAGEMENT FILE showing APPLIED PART temperatures not affected by operation of ME EQUIPMENT including SINGLE FAULT CONDITIONS; measurement of APPLIED PART temperature according to 11.1.3 not conducted
tests.result: Measurement of applied part temperature is conducted

tests.requirement: Surfaces of APPLIED PARTS cooled below ambient temperatures evaluated in RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS
Measurements not made when engineering judgment and rationale by MANUFACTURER indicated temperature limits could not exceed, as documented in RISK MANAGEMENT FILE
Test corner not used where engineering judgment and rationale by MANUFACTURER indicated test corner will not impact measurements, as documented in RISK MANAGEMENT FILE
Probability of occurrence and duration of contact for parts likely to be touched and for APPLIED PARTS documented in RISK MANAGEMENT FILE
tests.result: Risk management file has defined the probability of occurrence

products.name: PT9L
products.note: ME EQUIPMENT subject to IEC60601-1 safety testing

semantic_fragments.content: Internal pre-set controls not intended for adjustment during EXPECTED SERVICE LIFE of ME EQUIPMENT not taken into consideration. Verdict: N/A.

Under clause 11.1.2.2, APPLIED PARTS surface temperature exceeds 41°C must be disclosed in the instruction manual, including maximum temperature, conditions for safe contact (e.g. duration or condition of the PATIENT), and clinical effects with respect to characteristics such as body surface, maturity of PATIENTS, medications being taken or surface pressure documented in the RISK MANAGEMENT FILE. All sub-items were N/A for PT9L.

Radiation hazard clauses 10.2 through 10.7 all resulted in N/A (except 10.6 which passed) because PT9L has no X-radiation source, no alpha/beta/gamma/neutron particle radiation source, no intentional or unintentional microwave radiation source, no laser source, and no visible/infrared/ultraviolet electromagnetic radiation sources other than confirmed absence.
